description:
Found by the cold review of fz-5xp.3. NOT caused by it -- pre-existing.

    extern "C" fn libc::sqrt(float) :: float
    sqrt(9.0)

  fz2 interp -> 9.0        SILENTLY WRONG
  fz2 run    -> Cranelift verifier: arg 0 (v2) has type f64, expected i64

The interp leg is the bad one. `marshal_arg` passes the f64 via `to_bits()` in an
INTEGER register, because `dispatch_fn_returning` transmutes to
`fn(u64, ...) -> u64` per arity -- there is no float-lane dispatcher. The callee
reads a garbage xmm register, and the integer return register still holds the
argument's bits, which are read back as float bits. So it echoes its input, which
looks plausible and is not an error.

This is the same lane defect as fz-5xp.19 seen from the parameter side rather
than the return side; 19's repro is `(integer) :: float`, this one is
`(float) :: float`. Almost certainly one fix: the extern wrapper picks argument
lanes from the wrong place, and the interpreter's dispatchers have no float
lane at all. Fold with fz-5xp.19 when either is worked.

MATTERS BECAUSE fz-5xp.15 adds `fz_float_to_binary`, whose parameter is a float
lane, and Float formatting is on the JSON goal program's critical path.

DONE = a fixture declaring a float-lane extern that agrees on all three doors,
and the interpreter refusing rather than echoing if a lane is unsupported.
title: [BUG] A float-lane extern is broken differently in each door
